subject: Quantifying token ceilings and streaming impact for Acme POC
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Dana Lee <dana.lee@acme.com>, Josh Patel <josh@acme.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quantifying token ceilings and streaming impact for Acme POC

Hi Dana / Josh —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the specific asks we promised to follow up on so you can finish the internal SOW/PO work: 

Recap of constraints you shared: 
- Live operator chat use case, median incoming prompt ~600 tokens, occasional diagnostic attachments that add ~1,200 tokens.
- Target 95th-percentile latency <= 400ms for short replies (<= 200 output tokens); acceptable up to 800ms for long responses.
- Concurrent end-users expected peak: 220 live sessions; concurrency assumption today is ~0.25 requests/s per active session.
- Streaming required for reply drafts (server-side streaming of tokens to the client).

Ask list (actionable items):
1) We will validate three token-ceiling scenarios (input+output): 1k, 2k, 4k and provide expected p95 latency curves for each under your concurrency profile.
2) Dev request: can you confirm max attachment expansion (in tokens) and whether attachments must be included inline or can be stored and referenced?
3) Ops question: will you accept degraded outputs where we fall back to a smaller model for >95th-percentile events? (we suggested graceful fallback to quantized variants)
4) Please share a HubSpot or ticket link to the PO/Procurement owner so we can sync procurement milestones.

Attached: pooled_latency_matrix.csv (simulated curves based on our runtime benchmarking). I also uploaded the call recording to shared Drive (link below).

Next steps on our side: we'll run a short perf matrix (scenarios above) on a dedicated pool and share a one-page playbook: recommended model variant, batching settings, and streaming hedges (e.g., partial token flush every 200ms). Expect that by EOD tomorrow (your timezone).

If any of the constraints above are off, call it out and I can adjust the scenarios.

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
log an_wright@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pooled_latency_matrix.csv (csv stub), demo_recording.mp4 (video stub)
From: Dana Lee <dana.lee@acme.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Josh Patel <josh@acme.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T20:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quantifying token ceilings and streaming impact for Acme POC

Thanks Logan — useful recap. A few clarifications below: 

- Attachments: diagnostic attachments are pre-processed and we can provide them as references (we don't need inline expansion for all requests). Worst-case expansion is ~1,300 tokens for the largest diagnostic blob.
- Fallback: procurement would prefer deterministic behavior; we can accept fallback as long as there is a clear SLA/notice and a log of any fallback events.
- Concurrent sessions: peak 220 is correct; peak duration expected to be 30–45 mins in bursts.
- Streaming: must be true streaming for the operator UI (tokens as they generate); buffering of more than 300ms is unacceptable.

Questions for you:
1) Will you include KV-cache warmup guidance? We expect repeated turn-taking within a session, so cache hit rate matters.
2) Can you provide estimated token-cost delta between the 2k and 4k ceiling scenarios (rough $/1k tokens)?

I'll drop procurement contact in a follow-up once I confirm with our finance lead.

Dana Lee
Product Lead, Conversational Ops
Acme Robotics

Internal action items I propose:

- SRE (Grace): confirm autoscale thresholds and plausible buffer latency (esp under 220 concurrent sessions). Add a canary rule to route overflow to a lower-cost instance class with alerting.

Grace

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Dana Lee <dana.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quantifying token ceilings and streaming impact for Acme POC

Dana — appreciate the quick clarifications. Short answers below and next steps: 

- Attachments: good — we will treat attachments as references where possible. For the perf matrix we'll model both inline expansion (1,300 tokens) and reference flow to show delta.
- Fallback: we'll draft an SLA appendix that defines fallback events, notification windows, and a max monthly fallback budget.
- Streaming: we'll ensure token flushes no later than 200ms in our recommended config (we'll show results).
- KV-cache guidance: we'll include a short guide: cache-warmup pattern, suggested TTL, and how to prewarm for session reuse.
- Cost delta: we will include approximate $/1k-token numbers for each ceiling in the perf matrix.

Deliverables and timing: 
- By 2027-03-22 EOD PT: perf matrix with p50/p95/p99 latency for 1k/2k/4k ceilings, cost delta estimates, and streaming flush behavior.
- By 2027-03-25: draft SLA appendix and fallback runbook for your procurement review.

I attached the simulated latency matrix we discussed and uploaded the call recording here: https://drive.redwood/demo/acme-proc-recording.

If you'd like a short follow-up call to walk through the matrix when we deliver, I'm happy to schedule a 30-minute slot.

Best,
Logan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

> Attachments: pooled_latency_matrix.csv (simulated curves)
